title: Velero, by the risk it changes
summary: Backup and restore for Kubernetes resources and persistent volumes. Written as an answer, what an agent changes in a cluster can be partly undone, as of the last backup.

baseline.why: The model's typical deployment, with the answers this project addresses stated as they are without it: some of what it changes cannot be undone.

does.text: Backups of cluster resources and volumes, and restores.
does.quote: If the resource already exists in the target cluster

changes.why: Partly: as of the last backup, for Kubernetes resources and volumes only. A resource that still exists is skipped on restore unless an existing-resource policy says otherwise, which matters when the agent changed something rather than deleting it.

basis.quote: If the resource already exists in the target cluster

adds_note: A backup is a second copy of the data, and the credential that takes it can read everything in scope. Anything changed since the last backup is still lost.
adoption: Schedule backups often enough for the agent's rate of change.
Set the existing-resource policy, so an edit can be reverted and not only a deletion.
does_not_claim: That it was tested. Nothing was installed or run; every change rests on the documentation quoted beside it.
next: Published, and sent to the project's maintainers at the same time. If a change is wrong, or another answer should move, the case changes with the date they said so.
